## Phenomenon

Over an algebraically closed field of any prime characteristic, a single
$\mathbb G_a$ can act on affine space with a non-finitely generated invariant
ring. In the example below the group acts by simultaneous translations whose
coefficients are monomials. The invariant ring is the Cox ring of
$\overline M_{0,n}$, the moduli space of stable $n$-pointed rational curves.

## Setup

Let $n\ge 5$, write $[n-1]=\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$, and set
$$
R=k[y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1},(x_I)_{1\le |I|\le n-4}],
\qquad
z_i=\prod_{I\ni i}x_I,
$$
where the indices $I$ are subsets of $[n-1]$ in the stated size range.
Doran and Giansiracusa define the action by
$$
\rho(x_I)=x_I,\qquad \rho(y_i)=y_i+Tz_i.
$$
Since the $z_i$ are fixed, composing two substitutions adds the two parameters.
For $n\ge6$ the action is non-linearizable [@doran2014, Cor. 1.3].

The coefficient of $T$ is the derivation
$D^{(1)}=\sum_i z_i\partial/\partial y_i$. In characteristic $p$,
$D^{(1)}(y_i^p)=0$, while
$$
\rho(y_i^p)=y_i^p+T^pz_i^p.
$$
A polynomial $f$ is invariant if and only if the coefficient of $T^j$ in
$\rho(f)$ vanishes for every $j\ge1$. These coefficients come directly from the
binomial expansion of the substitution. Doran, Giansiracusa and Jensen turn
their vanishing into balancing conditions on weighted simplicial complexes
[@doran2017, Thm. 3.5].

## Construction

Invert every $x_I$ and write $u_i=y_i/z_i$. All the $u_i$ translate by $T$.
The differences $u_i-u_{n-1}$ are fixed, and the last coordinate
$u_{n-1}$ is a translation variable. Thus the invariants after localisation
are the polynomial ring in these differences over $k[x_I^{\pm1}]$.
Intersecting with $R$ gives the global invariant ring. The problem is which
polynomials in the differences, with Laurent coefficients in the $x_I$, lie in $R$.

## Proof of non-finite generation

Doran and Giansiracusa identify this intersection with
$\operatorname{Cox}(\overline M_{0,n})$, compatibly with the grading by
$\operatorname{Pic}(\overline M_{0,n})$ [@doran2014, Cor. 1.3]. Castravet,
Laface, Tevelev and Ugaglia show that for $n\ge10$ the pseudo-effective cone
of divisors on $\overline M_{0,n}$ is non-polyhedral, in characteristic zero
and in every prime characteristic [@castravet2023]. If the Cox ring were
finitely generated, it would be generated by finitely many homogeneous
elements. The effective cone would then be spanned by their degrees, hence
polyhedral and closed, and so equal to the pseudo-effective cone. So
$R^{\mathbb G_a}$ is not finitely generated for $n\ge10$.

## Outro

Weitzenböck's theorem concerns linear actions of a single $\mathbb G_a$ in
characteristic zero. This example keeps the group and drops linearity,
and the same failure occurs in characteristic zero as well. It marks the
boundary of the linear finite-generation question in positive characteristic.

## References and related examples

[Roberts' counterexample](../roberts/index.qmd) is another nonlinear action of a
single $\mathbb G_a$ with a non-finitely generated invariant ring, on
$\mathbb A^7$ in characteristic zero.

Doran, Giansiracusa and Jensen summarise the description of the Cox ring as a
ring of invariants in @doran2017 [Thm. 2.1].
